title: Hosted interaction slicing PRD — scope clarifications, acceptance criteria, and launch checklist
creator: Asha Patel
description: This PRD defines interaction-slicing for the hosted inference surface (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank). Interaction-slicing groups requests by behavioral characteristics and routes them to tuned lanes (fast-cost-optimized, quality-first, embeddings-only, rerank). Goal: reduce unit cost for common low-complexity traffic while preserving strict quality contracts for high-importance requests. The doc clarifies initial scope, a deliberate scope-reduction decision, acceptance criteria per slice, rollout plan with gated evals, telemetry requirements, and a launch checklist.
background_and_problem_statement: Customers have mixed workloads on a single endpoint: short prompts used for assistants, long-form creative generation, similarity queries for search, and dense reranking pipelines. Serving all with a single model/config wastes capacity or forces conservative latency SLAs. Interaction-slicing enables per-behavior policy: lighter quantized variants and aggressive batching for low-cost lanes, and higher-fidelity model variants for quality lanes. We must ship a minimal, low-risk implementation that is operable and observable for an initial launch.
in_scope: 1) Introduce interaction classification rules (client-supplied tags + heuristic classifier). 2) Implement lane routing for four lanes: fast-cost, standard, quality, embeddings/rerank. 3) Per-lane model pinning, batching policy, cache hints, and quantization profiles. 4) Eval harness and per-slice quality gates. 5) Console dashboards for per-lane latency, cost, error-rate, and quality regressions. 6) Canary rollout with traffic slicing and automated rollback triggers.
out_of_scope: 1) Tool-calling streaming API support for lane-aware routing (deferred). 2) Full private/VPC deployment parity in the first launch tranche. 3) Automatic model architecture conversion; teams will supply compatible model variants. 4) Dynamic per-request fine-grained KV cache switching (deferred to post-launch).
scope_changes_and_decisions: Initial draft included streaming & tool-calling on day-one. After risk review (2026-02-25), we scoped streaming/tool-calling out of the first launch to reduce verification surface and simplify telemetry. Quantization profiles will be recommended but not auto-applied; infra will surface a config knob. Decision log: keep classifier conservative (low false-positive rate for quality lane) and require client tag opt-in for cost-optimized lane until classifier M+2.
requirements: 1) Classification: deterministic rules + lightweight ML classifier with <3ms median inference. 2) Routing: route header/tag OR classifier result to one of four lanes. 3) Per-lane SLOs: latency p95 targets and per-token cost budget. 4) Model compatibility: each lane must accept identical API payloads and response schema. 5) Telemetry: token counts, cost estimate, latency distribution, lane attribution, cache hit rates, and per-prompt eval signals. 6) Eval gating: nightly regression checks against slice-specific prompt sets and acceptance thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: All four lanes reachable via the hosted API with a single boolean header and classifier fallback
Per-lane p95 latency achieved on testbed under representative load: fast-cost p95 <= 120ms, standard <= 250ms, quality <= 600ms, embeddings <= 180ms
Per-lane unit-cost estimate reported in telemetry and documented in Console within +/- 15% of observed invoice-cost in staging
Eval harness runs nightly for each lane; no critical quality regression (>3% metric drop) compared to baseline for gated launch
Canary rollout automation supports traffic slicing, ramp rules, and automatic rollback if error rate or quality gate triggers
Console dashboards show lane attribution, top failure reasons, and a per-prompt latency/cost heatmap
SLO/SLI definition doc published and acknowledged by SRE and Product (links provided)
metrics_and_telemetry: We will capture: lane_id, classification_reason (tag|classifier), model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, inferred_cost_usd, latency_ms (p50/p90/p95/p99), error_code, cache_hit, eval_score_delta. Export to metrics pipeline (Prometheus/Tempo/Tracing) and nightly aggregates to Data Warehouse for eval gating. Define a dashboard template and alert thresholds (error_rate > 0.5% sustained, p95 > target + 25%, eval regression > threshold).
eval_and_quality_gates: Per-lane prompt sets curated by PM + Research: short-help (fast-cost), conversational (standard), multi-turn reasoning (quality), semantic-similarity benchmarks (embeddings/rerank). Nightly compute per-task metrics (exact-match, BLEU-like heuristics, semantic-sim MRR). Gate rules: no gate may fail more than 1 consecutive night. If gate fails, stop canary ramp and create rollback runbook ticket. Evals must include randomized inputs to detect tokenization/regeneration differences.
rollout_plan: Pre-launch: run 7-day shadow traffic baseline for classifier & lane policies in staging
Canary phase 1: 1% global traffic to fast-cost lane for low-risk tenants (opt-in header) for 48 hours
Canary phase 2: 5% traffic ramp with standard+embeddings lanes for a controlled tenant set; run nightly evals
Canary phase 3: 25% traffic with quality lane enabled for high-SLA tenants only; run continuous monitoring
Full launch: enable lane routing globally with default conservative classifier; open opt-in for customers to tag traffic for fast-cost lane
Post-launch: schedule M+1 tasks to enable classifier-driven opt-in and to extend feature to Private tenants
launch_checklist: API contract: document header/tag schema and classifier fallback semantics (Confluence: hosted/interaction-slicing/contract)
SDK updates: add header helpers in JS/Python SDKs and unit tests (GH PR #18762)
Model onboarding: confirm model_variant artifacts for all lanes and quant profiles (SRE checklist)
Telemetry: dashboard template deployed and smoke alerts configured (Grafana dashboard ID 4221)
Eval harness: per-lane prompt sets created and nightly job green for 14 days
Canary automation: traffic-slicing feature flags ready and rollback playbook published
Operational runbooks: incident response, SLA/customer communication templates, escalation path to SRE & PM
Security & compliance: review for telemetry PII, KMS keys verified for model artifacts
Docs: Public API docs updated and examples for lane-tagging included
Support: internal playbook and FAQ for CSM/Support; training session scheduled
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: classifier misrouting could route quality-critical traffic to a cost lane. Mitigation: conservative classifier, require explicit client tag for cost lane during first 8 weeks, monitor misroute rate and implement corrective model updates. Risk: cost underestimation on quantized lanes. Mitigation: telemetry estimate and pre-launch load tests with invoicing reconciliation. Risk: eval metric blindspots. Mitigation: expand prompt corpus with adversarial examples and customer-supplied prompts during beta.
open_questions_and_action_items: Q: Should we expose lane selection via tokenized SDK flags or require header? A: Use header + SDK helper. Action: SDK owner to produce helper by 2026-03-22.
Q: Default traffic allocation for first-week global launch? A: Conservative — classifier off by default; require opt-in tags. Action: PM to finalize by 2026-03-18.
Q: Customer-facing pricing for cost lane? A: Pricing to be set by RevOps post-MVP. Action: coordinate with RevOps during M+1.
Q: Is rerank allowed to return top-K instead of scores for lane parity? A: Must preserve response schema. Action: Research to provide compatibility layer by 2026-03-30.
notes: This PRD prioritizes a conservative, observable first launch. After M+1 we iterate on classifier aggressiveness, expand streaming/tool-calling support, and enable Private parity. Keep communication tight with SRE for early signal handling.
